name: Topic 1: The Rise of Globalisation
summary:
{%:Introduction}

We live in a highly integrated and interdependent world. This chapter helps you understand the global nature of modern business, and the success of it depends not only on the domestic economic environment but also on the developments abroad. 

{%} {%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 1 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for topic 1

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Explain the characteristics of globalization and describe how it functions.
  • Identify how major international institutions facilitate globalization.
  • Evaluate the need for strong and transparent institutions to adapt to global competition.
  • Describe the key policy measures that make globalization sustainable.
  • Describe the role of information technology n bridging the global digital divide.
  • Describe the validity of the anti-globalization argument.
  • Explain the case made to temporarily support those people negatively affected by globalization.

{%}

name: Topic 3: Regional Economic Integration and The International Flow of Funds and Exchange Rates
summary:
{%:Introduction}

It is important to understand that regional integration is an ongoing process. Common reasons for regional integration are economic, political, or combination of both. Regional integration can bridge barriers between national borders, and increase interdependence within a region and the rest of the world.

This topic also discusses international trade patterns, examines the foreign exchange market, and discusses the behaviour of international currencies. This is because with the increasingly integrated world economy and financial markets, balance of payments accounts document trade and finance interactions between countries.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 3&4 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Explain regional economic integration, its evolution, and its benefits and costs.
  • Identify how economic geography helps explain, promote, and segment regional integration blocs.
  • Identify the primary reasons why countries are now seeking to pursue regional integration at the expense of multilateral trade liberalization.
  • Explain why the European Union is seen as the most advanced regional integration bloc.
  • Describe how NAFTA has affected U.S.–Mexico bilateral trade in goods and services.
  • Explain the importance of ASEAN and indicate why Asia may become the most important free trade region for this century.
  • Explain why regional integration in Latin America is challenging, and why there is potential for a grouping like MERCOSUR to become more predominant.
  • Explain the balance of payments for a country.
  • Describe the foreign exchange market and its components.
  • Discuss the development of international monetary systems.
  • Explain exchange rate changes over time.
  • Forecast exchange rates using different methodologies.

{%}

{%:Resources}

Essential textbook

Chapter 3&4, Gaspar 2017

Mini case: Iceland’s Economic Woes (Gaspar, pp111)

Recommended reading

Is the Chinese Renminbi Undervalued? (Gaspar, pp98)

Mini case: The European Union Sans Frontiere? (Gaspar, pp85)

name: Topic 5: The Legal and Political Environment
summary:
{%:Introduction}

International business needs to consider the legal and political systems that vary among different countries. Different kinds of laws may be stricter in some countries and more lax in others. In addition, doing business in some countries is fraught with legal and political risks. While the legal and political situation in some countries is very stable, in others widespread corruption and governmental expropriation of assets frequently occurs.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 6 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Provide an overview of the different global political systems and their potential impact on international business.
  • Explain the differences among communism, capitalism, and socialism and how these different economic ideologies affect the conduct of international business.
  • Discuss the key political and economic risks and the role of corruption when conducting global business.
  • Analyse the different types of legal systems and some key principles involving criminal, contract, tax, product safety, and dispute settlement law.
  • Discuss the importance of intellectual property protections in today’s global business environment and the major types of intellectual property protections, including patents, trademarks, and copyrights.

{%}

{%:Resources}

Essential textbook

Chapter 6, Gaspar 2017

Dumb Starbucks Coffee (Gaspar, pp161)

Recommended reading

Mini case: Becoming a King? (Gaspar, pp163)

name: Topic 6: Corruption and Ethics in Global Business
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Ethics affect the ways how people conduct business. It has become imperative for multinational corporations to understand how to conduct their business in ethics ways and how to be socially responsible. It is not always easy because of cultural and political differences among countries.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 7 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Explain briefly the meaning of ethics.
  • Describe how ethics and economic progress are connected.
  • Describe briefly the function of corporate social responsibility.
  • Recount the events in some of the more famous corporate financial scandals.
  • Explain how ethics can be taught.
  • Explain how internal controls can facilitate ethical behaviour and help prevent financial impropriety.

{%}

name: Topic 8: Control of Global Business
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Global corporations need to formulate different strategic approaches and control mechanisms for different countries of operations in order to succeed in their global business.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 9 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Discuss the importance of mission statements, and the difference between shareholder and stakeholder orientations in such statements and in general corporate strategy formulation.
  • Explain tactical versus operational plans in implementing corporate strategy, and Miles’ and Snow’s four basic types of longer-term strategic implementation.
  • Analyse various impediments to the coordination of strategic implementation that might exist for global businesses, and the positive role knowledge management and systems can play in this regard. In particular, discuss the role of tacit versus explicit knowledge, and that of the Internet.
  • Discuss and analyse various types of control systems utilized by global businesses including bureaucratic controls, interpersonal controls, output controls, and measurement systems such as six sigma initiatives.
  • Analyse the role organizations’ culture plays in controlling organizational activities, and how, when necessary, organizational cultures can potentially be changed.

{%}

{%:Resources}

Essential textbook

Chapter 9, Gaspar 2017

Royal Dutch Shell-A “Shell” in the Oil Industry (Gaspar, pp222)

Recommended reading

name: Topic 10: International HRM and International Marketing
summary:
{%:Introduction}

We will learn on the functional aspects of managing global business in the topics hereinafter. We start with two important aspects: international human resource management and international marketing.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 11&12 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Explain the basic cultural and regulatory issues involved in global human resource management including outsourcing and offshoring.
  • Describe the challenges involved in staffing foreign operations, assessing needs for training and development, and designing appropriate strategies to meet those needs.
  • Discuss performance appraisals and employee compensation issues around the world, including cultural differences, cost of living, and how expatriate issues are handled.
  • Distinguish between standardization and adaptation.
  • Describe how new products are developed and how existing products are managed for international markets.
  • Explain the four different methods of promoting international marketing products and provide some advantages and disadvantages of each.
  • Define channels of distribution and physical distribution and indicate the role of each of these for marketing products internationally.
  • Discuss the objectives and decisions involved in international pricing.
  • Discuss aspects of customer service required for goods and services that are globally marketed.

{%}

Essential textbook

Expatriates in Qatar (Gaspar, pp277)

name: Topic 12: Other Operational Perspectives of Global Business: Finance, Accounting and Taxation
summary:
{%:Introduction}

We will brief some other important aspects of international business in this topic, and understand some key concept and operational activities such as foreign exchange rate and its impact, financial and accounting report systems etc.

{%}

{%:Guidelines}

Read Chapter 14&15 of the text

Watch lecture recordings for the topic

Read the workshop case and participate in workshop discussions

Go through recommended readings

{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  • Explain how foreign exchange risk affects firms and investors.
  • Describe different ways to hedge exchange rate risk.
  • Discuss sources of funds to finance international trade and investment.
  • Discuss how exchange rate risk affects firms’ cash flows and its impact on stock returns.
  • Explain briefly the function of accounting and describe the two parts of the accounting information system.
  • Describe briefly the function of GAAP.
  • Recount the goal of the IASB and describe why IFRS are important to global business operations.
  • Explain how auditing contributes to the usefulness of financial reporting.
  • Explain how financial statement analysis can be used to evaluate a company’s financial situation and compare it to other companies.
  • Describe briefly tax issues that MNCs face.

{%}

{%:Resources}

Essential textbook

Chapter 14&15, Gaspar 2017


Recommended reading

Executive Compensation Rules in Financial Institutions (Gaspar, pp353)
